title: Span-compaction microbatcher with kernel-placement-aware grouping
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem statement:
Many requests have short remaining decode lengths relative to a common max-sequence slot, causing excessive zero-padding and suboptimal GPU kernel throughput. Current bucketing groups by coarse seqlen bins which reduces padding but still leaves fragmentation and kernel misalignment for attention kernels that prefer certain block sizes.

Goal:
Design and implement a 'span-compaction' microbatcher that compacts short sequences into contiguous token spans within GPU batch slots, uses kernel-placement heuristics to pack sequences into kernel-friendly granularities, and coordinates with prefill/decode scheduling to preserve KV cache locality and latency SLOs. The feature must be safe for hosted and dedicated deployments and opt-in behind a runtime flag for Canary rollout.
design_summary:
High-level approach:
1) Maintain a short-window lookahead queue for pending prefill requests (20ms or up to N requests).
2) Compute a packing score for each request: remaining_tokens, attention_pattern_hint (causal vs. masked), priority_tier, kernel_alignment_score (prefers multiples of 32/64 tokens depending on model dtype).
3) Use a greedy first-fit-decreasing-style bin pack inside each microbatch to co-locate sequences so that filled spans hit kernel-friendly lengths before padding to slot max.
4) Reserve contiguous KV cache ranges per packed span to avoid interleaved KV writes; update runtime KV index mapping.
5) Add a kernel-placement heuristic that biases grouping toward sequences whose combined shape triggers preferred CUDA kernel selection (e.g., multiples of 128 for fused-attn kernels).
6) Provide a fallback that preserves original order for high-priority low-latency requests to avoid head-of-line waits.

Trade-offs considered:
- Packing reduces padding but increases scheduling latency for some requests (bounded by lookahead window).
- More sophisticated bin packing yields diminishing returns vs. overhead. We choose a bounded greedy strategy to keep scheduler CPU cost low.
- KV reservation increases bookkeeping complexity and may fragment memory; mitigations include periodic compaction and reuse windows.
implementation_notes:
Planned repo changes:
- runtime/microbatcher: add span_compactor module with config knobs: lookahead_ms, max_lookahead_count, kernel_alignment_targets, priority_thresholds.
- runtime/kv_cache: expose APIs for reserve_span(request_id, start_slot, length) and commit_span/abort_span.
- scheduler: integrate packer in prefill path, ensure decode path reads span mappings.
- metrics: add pack_ratio, pad_tokens_saved, packing_latency_ms, pack_conflicts.

Backward compatibility:
- Feature gated by runtime flag `enable_span_compaction`. Default off for existing deployments.
- Provide telemetry-only mode: compute packing decisions but do not apply them (for offline verification).

Testing approach:
- Unit tests for packer correctness (no token loss, mapping correctness).
- Microbenchmarks on representative models (mix of Llama-2 and MPT-family) and dtypes (fp16/q4) on A100 and H100.
- End-to-end load test in dedicated pool with synthetic seqlen distributions (zipfian, bimodal) and with real customer traces (redaction applied).
acceptance_criteria:
- Implementation compiles and can be enabled via runtime flag.
- P95 decode latency regression <= 5% for 'high' priority tier under baseline load.
- For the target mixed workload (50% short seq < 16 tokens, 30% mid 16-128, 20% long >128) show >= 18% reduction in average pad tokens per request and >= 12% improvement in tokens/sec GPU utilization in microbench.
- Unit and integration tests in CI with simulated KV reservations.
- Rollout plan documented and safety toggles (max_lookahead_ms, per-tenant disable) implemented.
benchmarks_plan:
Benchmarks to run:
1) Controlled microbench: fixed batch size 64, compare baseline bucketing vs span-compaction across seq distributions (uniform, zipfian, bimodal). Collect tokens/sec, GPU active SM utilization, kernel selection histogram.
2) Latency SLO run: mixed priority traffic with 5ms p50 target; measure p50/p95/p99 prefill+decode.
3) Memory stress: long-running allocation test to detect KV fragmentation and compaction cost.
4) Canary on Dedicated: small customer-facing dedicated pool with telemetry-only mode first, then active compaction on 10% of traffic.

Artifacts and scripts:
- bench/scripts/pack_bench.py (param sweep), bench/results/README links in attachments.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1 (Dev): run microbenchmarks and unit tests locally.
Stage 2 (CI): run integration tests on the PR; add automated pad-savings regression check.
Stage 3 (Canary - telemetry-only): enable computation of packing decisions and surface metrics to console (no apply) for 48 hours.
Stage 4 (Canary - active): enable on 5% requests in a small dedicated pool for 72 hours, monitor pack_conflicts, p95 latency, and pad_tokens_saved.
Stage 5 (Ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback windows and per-tenant opt-out.
Safety knobs:
- max_lookahead_ms default 20, min 0.
- immediate bypass for priority >= P0.
- per-tenant feature_disable flag.
- telemetry alerts for pack_conflicts > 2% or packing_latency_ms > 30ms.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Increased head-of-line waiting causing latency spikes.
Mitigation: Strict lookahead bound and priority bypass; measure tail latencies during canary.

Risk: KV cache fragmentation and increased memory pressure.
Mitigation: implement reserve/commit/abort lifecycle and periodic compaction; cap total reserved spans per GPU.

Risk: Kernel-selection heuristics may regress for some models/dtypes.
Mitigation: maintain kernel-selection telemetry per model and allow model-specific alignment targets; ability to blacklist models from span compaction.

Risk: Scheduler CPU overhead and contention under extreme throughput.
Mitigation: keep packing algorithm O(n log n) with small N (lookahead cap 64), prefer in-place greedy packing, and allow sampling-based packing under large queue lengths.
metrics:
Primary metrics (instrumentation to add):
- pad_tokens_saved (sum over timeframe)
- pack_ratio = packed_tokens / total_pad_potential
- packing_latency_ms (time scheduler spends per microbatch)
- pack_conflicts (count of reserve failures requiring fallback)
- tokens_per_second (GPU-level improvement)
- p50/p95/p99 prefill+decode latency by priority tier
- kernel_histogram (which CUDA kernels invoked per microbatch)

Metric targets for canary:
- pad_tokens_saved >= 15% for representative mix
- packing_latency_ms p95 < 30ms
- pack_conflicts < 1%
